fact: APS reports that Senegalese startup Andakia presented Allo Goor Gi, an AI platform answering pupils' questions by phone call in Wolof and French without internet, built with the Ministry of National Education and hosted on servers in Senegal, according to its designer.
RTS says works began on 5 October 2026 on a locally run AI application for court archives, with an NVIDIA DGX Spark delivered, funded with UNDP and Korean support.

fact: Le Soleil reports that AI Hub Senegal, with the French embassy, presented on 2026-10-16 the Kiriku Voice challenge results: 210 hours of annotated Wolof, Pulaar and Serer speech data and two models, M-Kiriku ASR and M-Kiriku TTS, published openly on Hugging Face.

The higher-education ministry and a KOICA expert delegation met on the project to create an AI transformation centre at Diamniadio, to run 2026 to 2033 with an estimated investment of USD 14.5 million (about CFAF 8.22 billion), per RTS.

fact: APS reports that the Taouey supercomputer, bought by the Senegalese state from Atos in December 2019, was officially put into service in March 2024 at the Cite du savoir in Diamniadio, and is described as increasingly needed for training AI models.

CINERI's director general Ousmane Thiare says Taouey has had more than a hundred users since its start, and that public and private users, including scientists of the sub-region, can use its high-performance computing services.

CINERI director general Ousmane Thiare says the Taouey supercomputer is operational part-time, its second cell holding the GPU resources and often idled by power instability, while CPU resources are ready at full use.

Thiare says use of Taouey has been free and open to all since its arrival, with a webinar of over 200 online participants on 30 March 2026 and users named from UCAD's faculty of medicine and from environment and meteorology research.
Soynade released FineWeb-Wolof-50k, 50,000 rows of web text translated into Wolof with its Oolel-v0.1 model, on Hugging Face.

Senegal told the ITU in August 2026 of SENEGAL-AI, a language-model architecture being developed by the LITA laboratory of ESP, Cheikh Anta Diop University, resting on the CINERI Taouey supercomputer.
